---
title: "Env.SetString"
description: "Set a string value by key in the Env store."
---

Set the string value for `key`. `v` is truncated to 255 characters. `null` is stored as `""`. Silent no-op if the pool is full (256 entries).

## Signature

```enforce
static proto native void SetString(string key, string v);
```

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| key | `string` | The key to write. |
| v | `string` | The string value to store. Truncated to 255 chars; `null` becomes `""`. |

## Behavior

The store is locked. The kind is recorded as String. Overwriting a key of a different kind is allowed; the kind switches. Calling `SetString` on an existing String key invalidates any pointer previously returned by [Env.GetString](./getstring) on that key — make sure callers have already copied the prior string into a script-owned value before you overwrite.

## Edge cases

- Values longer than 255 characters are silently truncated.
- `null` becomes `""`.
- Writing past the 256-entry cap is a silent no-op.
- Cross-kind overwrite invalidates prior `GetString` pointers.

## Example

```enforce
Env.SetString("user", "admin");
```
